damageSigns: Rows of pinholes or shot holes on unfolding leaves
Bored stems, deadheart or broken stalks
pest.whyItMatters: Young larvae are most controllable before they tunnel into the maize stem, where surface treatment becomes ineffective.

inspectToday: Open the whorl on ten maize plants and check for fresh frass and young larvae.
Record how many plants show new shot holes or deadheart.
next48Hours: Destroy badly infested whorls or stems in a small local patch where practical.
Recheck newly damaged plants before larvae enter stems.
prevention: Remove infested stalk residues after harvest.
Use timely planting and locally recommended tolerant hybrids.
biologicalControl: Use a maize-labelled Bacillus thuringiensis product only while young larvae remain exposed in whorls.
Conserve parasitoids and predators by avoiding unnecessary broad-spectrum sprays.

pesticide.modeOfAction: Choose a maize-labelled product effective against exposed young borer larvae.
pesticide.resistanceNote: Rotate IRAC groups and do not treat old bored stems without fresh activity.
pesticide.labelRate: Use only the rate printed on a product registered for this crop and pest.
pesticide.application: Target active whorls at the label-approved stage before larvae enter the stem.
pesticide.interval: Reinspect for fresh frass and new shot holes before repeating.
pesticide.preHarvestInterval: Follow the product label and local agricultural-extension guidance.
pesticide.trigger: Use only when fresh whorl damage and live-larva counts cross local guidance.
pesticide.safety: Wear label-required PPE, avoid drift and water contamination, and never spray while pollinators are active.
pesticide.blockedReason: The Corn borer guide is not verified for Grape. Confirm with local extension.

damageSigns: Small wedge-shaped insects jumping from rice leaves
Virus-like stunting or discoloration in patches
pest.whyItMatters: Rice leafhoppers remove plant sap and some species can transmit rice diseases, so field distribution matters more than one photograph.

inspectToday: Sweep or tap ten rice hills and count leafhoppers at several points in the zone.
Check for spreading yellowing or virus-like symptoms.
next48Hours: Remove grassy volunteer hosts near nursery beds where practical.
Repeat sweep counts at the same time of day and compare the marked locations.
prevention: Use healthy seedlings and locally recommended resistant varieties.
Keep bund weeds managed while preserving beneficial insects.
biologicalControl: Conserve spiders, egg parasitoids and predatory bugs.
Avoid broad-spectrum spraying when counts are low and natural enemies are active.

pesticide.modeOfAction: Select a registered product only after the leafhopper species and crop stage are confirmed.
pesticide.resistanceNote: Rotate IRAC groups and avoid calendar treatment.
pesticide.labelRate: Use only the rate printed on a product registered for this crop and pest.
pesticide.application: Treat only confirmed hotspots at the label-approved rice stage.
pesticide.interval: Repeat standardized sweep or hill counts before another treatment.
pesticide.preHarvestInterval: Follow the product label and local agricultural-extension guidance.
pesticide.trigger: Use when local counts or confirmed disease-vector risk reach extension guidance.
pesticide.safety: Wear label-required PPE, avoid drift and water contamination, and never spray while pollinators are active.
pesticide.blockedReason: Retake the photo or obtain expert confirmation before selecting a pesticide.

damageSigns: Colonies on tender shoots or leaf undersides
pest.whyItMatters: Aphids multiply rapidly, weaken new growth and can transmit plant viruses.

inspectToday: Count colonies on five tender shoots in the selected zone.
Check for ladybirds, lacewings and parasitised aphid mummies before spraying.
next48Hours: Wash small colonies from sturdy plants with water.
Remove only badly curled, localised shoots and recount tomorrow.
prevention: Control weed hosts and inspect new seedlings before transplanting.
biologicalControl: Use crop-labelled insecticidal soap or neem on small colonies.

pesticide.modeOfAction: Select an active ingredient registered for the crop and aphid species.
pesticide.resistanceNote: Rotate IRAC groups and preserve natural enemies.
pesticide.labelRate: Use only the rate printed on a product registered for this crop and pest.
pesticide.application: Target confirmed colonies, especially leaf undersides; avoid whole-field treatment when infestation is local.
pesticide.interval: Recount colonies before any repeat treatment.
pesticide.preHarvestInterval: Follow the product label and local agricultural-extension guidance.
pesticide.trigger: Spray only when repeat counts rise above the crop-specific threshold and natural enemies are insufficient.
pesticide.safety: Wear label-required PPE, avoid drift and water contamination, and never spray while pollinators are active.
pesticide.blockedReason: The Aphids guide is not verified for Grape. Confirm with local extension.
